::: {.why}
The split you estimated last night is what decides whether trading slowly helps, and it is the parameter that separates a soluble execution problem from an insoluble one.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Separate temporary from permanent impact empirically and report the fraction that decays.
- Say what each component costs you and which one splitting an order can avoid.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit the decay: for large trades, model the impact path as a permanent level plus a temporary component decaying at some rate, and estimate both from your data. Report the permanent fraction and the decay half-life. Both feed directly into tomorrow's execution problem.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Draw the consequence: permanent impact is a cost you pay regardless of how you trade, because it is the market learning from you, while temporary impact is avoidable by trading slower. That asymmetry is the whole reason execution scheduling exists and it is worth stating in one sentence.
:::
:::
